title: Biblical Role Transfer & Canonical Reversal Ledger
purpose: Track when a theological function persists while its carrier, scale or social form changes across the biblical canon. Also track large beginning/end reversals such as guarded Tree access becoming restored/open Life in Revelation. This prevents naive word matching and makes canonical development visible.
epistemic_rule: This is an archive-level canonical reading. Individual biblical books retain distinct historical contexts and theological emphases. 'Transfer' means a later text reuses or transforms an earlier function/motif; it does not imply that all authors consciously shared one modern diagram.

role_transfers.changed_carrier: sacred landscape → portable sanctuary → building/city → person → people/community → city/creation scale
role_transfers.project_value: Supports a dynamic Presence theology rather than treating House/Temple as one fixed object.

role_transfers.changed_carrier: place → lineage/dynasty → sanctuary → eschatological dwelling → reconciled community → civic-sacred order
role_transfers.project_value: Makes Father's House relational and multi-register rather than reducible to one anatomical/geometric localization.

role_transfers.changed_carrier: memorial marker → promised foundation → rejected/reversal image → messianic foundation → participatory community structure
role_transfers.project_value: Rejected Stone is strongest when it becomes structural relation, not merely a personal-vindication slogan.

role_transfers.project_value: Explains why Ladder, Door and Way can belong to one access family without being literally identical objects.

role_transfers.preserved_function: life-giving provision flowing from sacred/source relation
role_transfers.changed_carrier: garden geography → wilderness gift → temple restoration → personal/Spirit metaphor → eschatological city river
role_transfers.project_value: River is a source-to-world operator: the center is judged by whether life moves outward.

canonical_reversals.ending: Tree of Life in New Jerusalem with healing fruit/leaves
canonical_reversals.theological_meaning: lost access to life is restored in transformed creation

canonical_reversals.ending: nations enter holy city; gates remain open under its own purity/order conditions
canonical_reversals.theological_meaning: exile/guarded boundary becomes reconciled civic participation

canonical_reversals.ending: no more curse; healing and divine face/presence
canonical_reversals.theological_meaning: restoration is not only access but transformation of the condition of life

canonical_reversals.ending: no separate temple in city because God and Lamb are its temple
canonical_reversals.theological_meaning: divine-presence architecture expands beyond a restricted inner chamber

canonical_reversals.theological_meaning: access to God and reconciliation among people are coupled rather than separable

methodological_laws: Function-before-form: prioritize what a motif does before comparing shapes/names.
Carrier-transfer: the same theological function may migrate from place to person to community to city.
Scale-expansion: later texts can universalize or enlarge earlier sacred-space patterns without making every stage identical.
Participation-expansion: mature presence theology increasingly includes a people/community rather than only a sacred object or leader.
Canonical-reversal: beginning/end correspondences are strongest when the later text explicitly reuses earlier vocabulary such as Tree, curse, city, river, light or presence.
Countertext rule: a proposed project mapping weakens when it requires role distribution or ethical direction opposite to the biblical sequence.
